response.text:
I can’t invent a precise percentage without the underlying data. Making up a number would be misleading.

What I can do instead (pick one):
- Tell you exactly how to calculate it if you can provide the raw counts (or the data file).
- Give a reproducible SQL query or spreadsheet formula you can run on your data.
- Produce a clearly labeled hypothetical example so you can see the math.
- Suggest methods to estimate it from partial data (sampling, last-quarter trend projection) and the caveats.

Quick checklist and formula you can use
- Define period: which dates are “last quarter” (e.g., Q2 2026 = 2026-04-01 to 2026-06-30)?
- Define the denominator: all users eligible to renew during that quarter (e.g., subscriptions with renewal date in the period).
- Define the numerator: among those, users who completed renewal in the period (manual or auto—specify).
- Formula: renewal_rate (%) = (renewed_users / eligible_users) × 100

Example SQL (replace table/column names)
SELECT 
  COUNT(CASE WHEN renewed = true THEN 1 END) AS renewed_users,
  COUNT(*) AS eligible_users,
  100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN renewed = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS renewal_rate_pct
FROM subscriptions
WHERE renewal_date >= 'YYYY-MM-DD' AND renewal_date < 'YYYY-MM-DD';

Spreadsheet formula (assuming renewed count in A1 and eligible count in B1)
=IF(B1=0,"N/A",A1/B1*100)

Hypothetical example (not real data)
- eligible_users = 5,000; renewed_users = 3,450
- renewal_rate = 3,450 / 5,000 × 100 = 69.0%

Tell me which quarter/date range you mean and whether you can share the counts or a file (or paste a sample of the data). I’ll compute the precise percent or give the exact query/script you can run.
